paper.title: Describe, Explain, Plan and Select: Interactive Planning with Large Language Models Enables Open-World Multi-Task Agents
paper.central_claim: DEPS - an event-triggered descriptor, an LLM that explains failures and re-plans, and a trained horizon-predictive goal selector - makes zero-shot LLM planning reliable for long-horizon open-world tasks: the first zero-shot multi-task agent that robustly accomplishes 70+ Minecraft tasks with nearly doubled overall performance, the first planning-based agent to reach diamond, and generally effective in ALFWorld and tabletop manipulation.
paper.scope_note: Scope flag for Opus: the main embodiment is a Minecraft avatar (game environment) with a learned goal-conditioned controller; ALFWorld (text world) and a CLIPort UR5e tabletop simulation appear only in the appendix. Kept in scope as simulated embodied-agent planning; the fit to 'robot' bodies is indirect.

evidence.quote: Our experiments mark the milestone of the first zero-shot multi-task agent that can robustly accomplish 70+ Minecraft tasks and nearly double the overall performances.
evidence.support_explanation: Central claim with its robustness wording.

evidence.quote: even when the Oracle controller is used, the success rate of executing Minecraft tasks is much less than that of the other environments.
evidence.support_explanation: Gap evidence: planner-side failure in open worlds even with oracle control (Fig 1 values not in text).

evidence.quote: Prior works mostly focus on solving the first challenge by providing environmental feedback to the LLM through affordance functions [ 4 ] , success detector [ 20 ] or scene descriptor [ 17 ] .
evidence.support_explanation: Lineage: affordance (SayCan), success detector (CaP), scene descriptor (Inner Monologue).

evidence.quote: we found it could still suffer from accumulative planning error, especially in long-horizon open-world tasks
evidence.support_explanation: Residue of the closest neighbour (Inner Monologue).

evidence.quote: whenever the controller fails to complete a sub-goal, a descriptor will summarize the current situation as text and send it back to the LLM-based planner.
evidence.support_explanation: Hand-back trigger and feedback channel.

evidence.quote: we take the symbolic information available in the game and translate it into feedback description
evidence.support_explanation: Descriptor reads symbolic game state (inventory, biome etc.), not images; alternatives (human, CLIP) are named but not used.

evidence.quote: Thus, the Success Detector can be implemented by monitoring changes in object information within the item inventory.
evidence.support_explanation: In-loop success detection reads inventory state (simulator-provided).

evidence.quote: we implement a horizon-predictive selector that embeds practical task experience to accurately rank the goals based on their efficiency and feasibility
evidence.support_explanation: Selector design: learned remaining-steps predictor ranks parallel goals.

evidence.quote: the horizon predictive selector can be jointly trained with the controller policies and share the backbone parameters
evidence.support_explanation: Selector is trained from offline controller trajectories; data size and source split not given.

evidence.quote: To minimize performance variation caused by the low-level controller, we standardize all experiments with one controller learned by behavior cloning.
evidence.support_explanation: Controller held fixed across methods.

evidence.quote: We choose 71 tasks from the Minecraft Universe Benchmark SkillForgeChain [ 22 ] for evaluation.
evidence.support_explanation: Task set.

evidence.quote: Since these methods were not originally experimented with Minecraft, we reproduce them to conform to the Minecraft specification based on prompt and feedback template design.
evidence.support_explanation: Baselines are author re-implementations.

evidence.quote: text-davinci-03 model [ 32 ] for GPT, CoT, and IM, and code-davinci-02 model [ 8 ] for PP, CaP, and Ours
evidence.support_explanation: Baseline LLMs differ: IM, CoT and GPT use text-davinci, DEPS uses code-davinci - a confound for the IM comparison; CaP and PP match.

evidence.quote: Every task is executed 30 times and the average results in Minedojo [ 10 ] for every meta task are listed in Table 2 .
evidence.support_explanation: Trial count per task (71 tasks x 30 = 2130 episodes per method).
DEPS per meta-task and average 48.56.
Strongest baseline (same code-davinci LLM) average 25.77: DEPS/CaP = 1.88x; other baselines 15.42-21.64.
DEP (no selector) average 39.36; selector adds +9.2.

evidence.quote: Starting from MT6, almost all existing LLM-based planners fail (nearly 0 success rate).
evidence.support_explanation: Hard tasks remain mostly unsolved; DEPS MT6-MT8 are 13.80 / 12.56 / 0.59.

evidence.quote: using our horizon-predictive Selector compared to not any selector
evidence.support_explanation: Selector ablation versus fixed, random, MineCLIP and CLIP selectors over 2-4 parallel goals; gains +22.3 / +29.2 / +32.6 points over no selector (figure values only in text).
Re-planning rounds ablation (0,1,3,5,inf): success rises monotonically; round 0 equals the vanilla planner.

evidence.quote: The maximum number of rounds for Codex is around 7-8 rounds.
evidence.support_explanation: Only call-budget information: re-planning limited by LLM token window; no per-task LLM calls, tokens or cost.
Baseline vs DEPS per LLM (Codex 28.6->79.8, GPT-3 27.2->75.4, ChatGPT 20.3->70.2, GPT-4 49.2->89.3): gain on four LLMs; the text's 'almost identical' DEPS success across LLMs is an overstatement.

evidence.quote: Since we use pretrained LLM as a planner, it indeed requires exposure to a large amount of Minecraft-related corpus during the pretraining phase.
evidence.support_explanation: Authors concede dependence on Minecraft knowledge in LLM pretraining (contamination/prior).

evidence.quote: How to obtain 1 wooden_button in Minecraft step - by - step ?
evidence.support_explanation: In-context demonstration uses wooden_button (and stone_sword), both of which are in the evaluated 71-task set (Table 21), so demos overlap with test tasks; baselines share the same demonstrations.
wooden_button is an evaluation task also used as an in-prompt demonstration; per-task rates are multiples of 1/30.

evidence.quote: All tasks are executed for at least 30 times across different world seeds, given the same initial conditions.
evidence.support_explanation: Per-task denominator is 'at least 30'; the headline ObtainDiamond 0.59% (Sec 4.4) cannot be a multiple of 1/30 so its denominator is not stated.

evidence.quote: our agent achieves a 0.59% success rate within 10 minutes of gameplay.
evidence.support_explanation: Diamond result: 0.59%, versus other methods cited at 0.1% (RL), 20% (VPT) and 2% (DreamerV3 in a modified environment).

evidence.quote: The primary bottleneck impeding overall agent success rate lies within the goal-conditioned Controller, not the plans generated by DEPS.
evidence.support_explanation: Oracle controller gives 60% on ObtainDiamond vs 0.6% with the BC controller: planner is not the binding limit on hard tasks.

evidence.quote: For better demonstrate the effectiveness of self-explanation in DEP, we also augment the zero-shot planner with re-planning ability (GPT+RP).
evidence.support_explanation: Only controlled test of explanation vs plain re-planning, in ALFWorld.

evidence.quote: candidate language-conditioned actions for each state
evidence.support_explanation: ALFWorld planner/controller receive text observations and admissible actions per state (privileged channel).
ALFWorld (10 tasks x 5 runs): BUTLER 37.0, GPT 10.0, GPT+RP 52.0, IM 30.0, DEP 76.0.
Tabletop (5 tasks x 5 runs): CLIPort+oracle 76.0, GPT 80.0, IM 56.4, DEP 80.0 - no gain over the zero-shot GPT planner.
DEPS on MineRL (Steve-1 controller) per meta-task; no baselines run there; MT3 62.4 -> 24.3.

evidence.quote: some previous fundamental challenges in planning (e.g., dead ends) may not prevalent in our adopted environments and hence could be inadvertently overlooked by our paper
evidence.support_explanation: Authors' scope caveat.

signatures.object: Interactive re-planning loop around a zero-shot code-style LLM planner: descriptor -> explainer -> re-planner.
signatures.information: Initial plan is a Python-like program with per-step preconditions/effects; on failure the descriptor feeds back a text summary of plan-relevant symbolic game state (inventory, biome etc., game-provided); the explainer prompt sees the failed action and inventory.
signatures.operation: Controller runs goals sequentially; a failed goal triggers description d_t, LLM self-explanation e_t, and re-plan P_t over the accumulated dialogue prompt p_t = CONCAT(p_{t-1}, d_t, e_t).
signatures.output: Revised goal sequence passed to a goal parser and the goal-conditioned BC controller.
signatures.conditions: Rounds bounded by the LLM token window (about 7-8 for Codex); two few-shot DEP demonstrations; symbolic game feedback available.
signatures.feedback: game-provided inventory/event info translated to text; success detector from inventory changes
signatures.selection_rule: not_applicable: single revised plan per round, no candidate pool.
signatures.persistence: within-episode dialogue only; nothing is kept across tasks.
signatures.claimed_effect: DEP (without selector) 39.36 average vs best baseline CaP 25.77; success rises monotonically with re-planning rounds (MT1 28.6 -> 79.8).
signatures.failure_boundary: Hard tasks MT6-MT8 (<=13.8%) limited by the BC controller; token window caps rounds.

signatures.object: Goal selector ranking parallel executable goals in the plan by predicted remaining horizon.
signatures.information: Current observation/state and candidate goal text; trained on offline trajectories (source and size of trajectories not stated in the paper text), backbone shared with the controller.
signatures.operation: Predict horizon distribution mu(h | s, g) and choose the goal with the smallest expected remaining steps (softmax over -mu).
signatures.output: Order/choice among parallel goals, modifying the plan.
signatures.conditions: Only when the plan contains alternative or order-free goals; limited episode length makes efficiency matter.
signatures.feedback: none at run time beyond the current state
signatures.selection_rule: argmax of exp(-mu(g,s)) over executable goals G_t.
signatures.later_use: used on each decision step of later tasks
signatures.claimed_effect: DEP 39.36 -> DEPS 48.56; +22.3 / +29.2 / +32.6 points over no selector at 2/3/4 parallel goals; beats CLIP/MineCLIP selectors.
signatures.failure_boundary: Needs a controller-aligned dataset; gains concentrated on efficiency-sensitive tasks (MT7).

gap.author_gap: (1) One-shot or weakly-corrected LLM plans fail on long open-world tasks needing 13+ ordered sub-goals; success-detector or scene-description feedback does not locate the plan error. (2) Plans ignore how reachable each alternative sub-goal is from the current state, making them infeasible or inefficient.
gap.checked_gap: Supported: Inner Monologue and other feedback planners are run on the same 71 tasks with the same controller and collapse from MT3 onward; DEPS ablations (rounds, selector variants) address each gap separately. Figure 1's oracle-controller evidence cannot be checked in text.
lineage: Zero-shot planner [16] / Chain-of-Thought [45] -> SayCan [4] (affordance), Code-as-Policies [20] (success detector, pythonic), ProgPrompt [42] (pythonic prompts), Inner Monologue [17] (scene descriptor + success detection) -> DEPS (precondition-annotated plan + failure explanation + horizon selector)
gap.closest_adjacent: Inner Monologue and Code-as-Policies re-implemented in Minecraft (IM on a weaker text-davinci LLM; CaP on the same code-davinci LLM).
gap.residue: Locating and repairing a wrong precondition in a long plan from execution feedback, and choosing efficient routes among equivalent sub-goals.
gap.stakes: Task completion within bounded episode lengths in open-world environments.
gap.method_response: Add failure descriptions, LLM self-explanation and re-planning, plus a learned reachability-aware selector.
gap.remaining_gap: Controller bottleneck on hard tasks (ObtainDiamond 60% with oracle vs 0.6% with BC); symbolic feedback unavailable on camera-only robots; explanation vs description not separated in Minecraft.
gap.current_relevance: Not assessed from later work; no later paper in the pinned local set bears on it.
unresolved: Figure 1 oracle-controller numbers are not in the pinned text.
Source and size of selector training trajectories are unstated.

matches.tactic_steps_checked: C25 step1 responsibility boundary: yes (LLM plans/explains; controller executes; selector scores). Step2 typed machine-checkable artifact: yes (code-style plan with preconditions/effects parsed to controller skills). Step3 close the loop with an obtainable signal mid-construction: yes (inventory-based success/failure plus description). Step4 ablate the loop: yes (rounds, selector variants; explanation only in ALFWorld). Step5 cost and confounds: cost absent, baselines on different LLMs, symbolic privileged feedback acknowledged.
matches.success_failure_checks: Success: closed-loop signals obtainable by the system - partial (game symbols). Success: single load-bearing mechanism ablated to a named baseline - partial (DEP vs IM/GPT+RP confounded). Failure: cost of delegation unmeasured - present; failure: baselines re-implemented per benchmark - present; failure: only marginal over unified baseline - absent.
matches.reason: The operation is a planner/controller/selector decomposition around typed plan artifacts with execution-fed correction, which is the decompose-and-delegate move; the executor is a learned BC controller and the checker is an inventory predicate rather than a sound solver, so only partial.

rs_pattern.reason: Primary fit to decompose_and_delegate; conditioning few-shot demos are scaffolding and not the claimed mechanism, so no supporting card is added.

executes_pattern.reason: Plan artifact, execution feedback loop and a learned selector are implemented and ablated, but the explanation component is isolated only in a 10-task ALFWorld test.

resolves_problem.reason: Success on mid-difficulty tasks rises substantially (MT3-MT5) but MT6-MT8 stay at or below 14% and diamond at 0.59%; the controller, not the planner, is the limiting factor there.

condition_checks.note: Hand-back fires on a game-state success/failure predicate and more rounds help monotonically, but the detector is exact only because it reads simulator inventory.
Detector reads privileged simulator state; paper names human/CLIP descriptors as alternatives but does not test them.
Planner gains are bounded by controller fidelity (60% oracle vs 0.6% BC on diamond).
Selector vs no selector compared in closed loop (DEP vs DEPS; fixed/random/CLIP/MineCLIP/HPS), but candidates are plan-parallel goals rather than sampled actions.
Selector ablation figure values only partly in text; 30-run tasks but constructed parallel-goal tasks.

unassigned: Descriptor -> LLM self-explanation -> re-plan dialogue with precondition-annotated code plans (no card; K202 covers only the hand-back timing, K203 needs a post-hoc diagnostic program).
revision_proposals: Pending, not applied: a failure-explanation-and-replan sub-pattern under external_verification_control (2302.01560; 2212.04088 is a lighter instance with observed-object re-prompting). Needs an independent second reading before candidate_pattern. R06 fit is structural only (candidate set = plan-parallel goals); consider a separate 'learned ranker over harness-made goal candidates' note rather than widening R06.

pattern_mapping.operation_correspondence: Controller executes typed sub-goals until a game-state predicate reports failure, then control returns to the LLM with a state description, and the LLM revises the remaining plan.
pattern_mapping.conditions_and_differences: K202 assumes a completion/stagnation monitor; here the monitor is exact because it reads inventory, and the hand-back additionally triggers an LLM self-explanation that K202 does not describe.

pattern_mapping.operation_correspondence: A learned scorer picks the best among candidate goals before execution.
pattern_mapping.conditions_and_differences: R06 samples action candidates from a policy and scores them with a verifier; DEPS scores plan-parallel goals by predicted remaining horizon (efficiency/feasibility, not correctness), so the correspondence is structural.

claims.text: DEPS nearly doubles the success of existing LLM planners on 71 Minecraft tasks with the same controller.
claims.setting: MineDojo 1.11.2, empty inventory, behaviour-cloned goal-conditioned controller, 71 tasks in 8 meta groups, 30 runs per task
claims.baseline_control: GPT zero-shot, ProgPrompt, CoT, Inner Monologue, Code-as-Policies (author re-implementations; GPT/CoT/IM on text-davinci, PP/CaP/DEPS on code-davinci)
claims.selection_vs_test: Prompt design and two in-context demonstrations (wooden_button, stone_sword) come from the evaluated task family; selector trained on controller trajectories of unspecified origin.
claims.result_denominator: Average 48.56 (DEPS) vs 25.77 (CaP), 21.64 (IM), 18.89 (CoT), 16.88 (PP), 15.42 (GPT); about 2130 episodes per method; MT6-MT8: 13.80 / 12.56 / 0.59
counterevidence: MT6+ near zero so 'robustly 70+ tasks' is an overstatement
claims.allowed_conclusion: On the authors' Minecraft task suite and controller, DEPS roughly doubles the average success of the same-LLM best baseline (1.88x) and raises mid-difficulty tasks substantially; hard tasks remain largely unsolved.

claims.text: The horizon-predictive selector improves plan efficiency.
claims.setting: Minecraft with 2-4 parallel candidate goals; Task101 DEP vs DEPS
claims.baseline_control: fixed, random, MineCLIP, CLIP selectors; DEP (no selector)
claims.result_denominator: 39.36 -> 48.56 average; +22.3/+29.2/+32.6 points over no selector (curves only in figure)
claims.allowed_conclusion: A learned remaining-horizon ranker helps in this environment where parallel goals have different distances; transfer to other embodiments is untested.

claims.setting: Minecraft re-planning rounds 0..inf; ALFWorld GPT+RP vs DEP
claims.result_denominator: MT1 28.6 -> 79.8 with rounds; ALFWorld avg GPT+RP 52.0 vs DEP 76.0 (10 tasks x 5 runs)
counterevidence: ALFWorld feedback and admissible actions are privileged text
claims.allowed_conclusion: More feedback-driven re-planning rounds help monotonically; the extra value of the LLM's explanation beyond plain re-planning is supported only by a small ALFWorld test.

claims.text: DEPS is effective in non-open-ended ALFWorld and tabletop manipulation.
claims.setting: ALFWorld text world 10 tasks x 5 runs; CLIPort UR5e simulated tabletop 5 tasks x 5 seeds
claims.selection_vs_test: prompts and descriptors re-engineered per environment
counterevidence: tabletop shows no gain over zero-shot GPT
all methods get 0% on Pick Two
claims.allowed_conclusion: Small-scale simulated tests show gains in ALFWorld and parity in tabletop; not evidence of general effectiveness.

claims.text: First planning-based agent to reach diamond in Minecraft.
claims.baseline_control: cited RL/VPT/DreamerV3 numbers from other papers
claims.result_denominator: 0.59% (denominator not stated; not a multiple of 1/30); 60% with an oracle controller (denominator not stated)
claims.allowed_conclusion: A planner-driven pipeline reached a diamond in rare runs; the rate is far below prior imitation/RL systems and its denominator is unreported.

assessment.evidence_level_reason: Closed-loop simulator success in Minecraft (environment-checked item acquisition) with repeated runs; feedback reads simulator symbolic state, demos overlap evaluation tasks, and the ALFWorld/tabletop extensions use per-environment prompts, small task counts and text-world privileged actions, so no transfer level is granted (anchor precedent 1).
assessment.strongest_supported_claim: With a fixed behaviour-cloned controller and simulator-symbolic feedback, DEPS (descriptor, explainer, re-planner and a learned goal selector) raises average success on the authors' 71-task Minecraft suite from about 26% for the strongest same-LLM re-implemented baseline to 48.6%, mostly on short-to-medium tasks, with monotone gains from re-planning rounds; 'robust on 70+ tasks', 'general effectiveness' and the diamond result are not supported at the strength claimed.
assessment.reproduction: author_report only; no reproduction by us

G.reason: Two distinct, sourced gaps (flawed long plans that feedback alone does not repair; plans blind to sub-goal reachability), explicit lineage across zero-shot, CoT, SayCan, CaP, ProgPrompt and Inner Monologue, all run on the same tasks, and a bounded residual (controller bottleneck, missing explanation isolation).

M.reason: Precondition-annotated plans enable error localisation, the explainer targets the stated cause, the selector targets reachability, and rounds/selector give distinguishable predictions. Weak assumption: the value of LLM explanation over plain re-planning is argued but tested only in a tiny ALFWorld setting, and feedback assumes symbolic state.

X.reason: Equation (1), full prompts and dialogue, descriptor, parser, success detector, token-bounded rounds and controller details are given; failure boundaries (controller, token window, LLM dependence) are discussed. Not 4: selector training data/size, how plan candidates are formed for the selector, and descriptor construction beyond inventory are thin.

measurement.reason: Success is MineDojo's programmatic item check, 30 runs per task with per-task rates in Appendix F; weaker points: the diamond and oracle-controller rates have no denominators, the in-loop detector and descriptor read simulator state, and sd is across tasks.

causality.reason: Five baselines on the same controller, selector variants, round ablation and an LLM sweep give broad evidence. Confounds remain: IM/CoT/GPT use a different LLM, baselines are re-implemented, the explainer is not toggled in Minecraft, the descriptor carries privileged symbolic state, and the 'LLMs give almost identical results' statement conflicts with Table 19.

holdout.reason: Two in-context demonstrations are evaluation tasks, prompts and selector were built on the same task family, Minecraft pretraining exposure is conceded, and the ALFWorld/tabletop extensions use re-engineered components with small task sets (tabletop gain zero). Different Minecraft versions/controllers are a mild robustness check without baselines.

statistics.reason: 30 runs per task and sd across tasks plus a per-task table, but no seed-level variance, paired tests or failure decomposition for the planner; extension environments use 5 runs with no variance.

cost.reason: Episode step caps and the controller are shared and re-planning is bounded (about 7-8 rounds), so the call budget is derivable only roughly; no calls, tokens, latency or dollars are reported, and the privileged symbolic descriptor channel is not priced.

status_reason: Complete full text with appendices read; all eight items judged; scope flag recorded for Minecraft.
